title_en: Xiamen International Bank v. Jinjiang Houtai Shoes Industry Co., Ltd. and Jinjiang Xiaosheng Garment Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract

full_text_en:
Xiamen International Bank v. Jinjiang Houtai Shoes Co., Ltd. and Jinjiang Xiaosheng Garment Industrial Co., Ltd. — dispute over a loan contract

Plaintiff: Xiamen International Bank, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Ziying, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant: Jinjiang Houtai Shoes Co., Ltd., Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Li Jiangning, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant: Jinjiang Xiaosheng Garment Industrial Co., Ltd., Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Liangxing, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, Xiamen International Bank, Fujian Province (hereinafter referred to as "International Bank"), filed an action with the Siming District People's Court of Xiamen, Fujian Province, against the defendants, Jinjiang Houtai Shoes Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Houtai Company") and Jinjiang Xiaosheng Garment Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Xiaosheng Company"), due to a dispute over a loan contract.

The plaintiff, International Bank, alleged: On March 30, 1994, the plaintiff made a loan of HKD 800,000 to the defendant Houtai Company, and the defendant Xiaosheng Company provided joint and several liability guarantee for this loan. After the loan matured, Houtai Company only repaid the loan interest up to December 31, 1995, and the remaining principal and interest have not been paid to date; Xiaosheng Company also did not assume the guarantee liability. The plaintiff requested a judgment ordering Houtai Company to repay the loan principal, interest, and default interest, and ordering Xiaosheng Company to assume joint and several guarantee liability.

The defendant Houtai Company did not submit a defense.

The defendant Xiaosheng Company argued: On August 21, 1995, the defendant notified the plaintiff in writing by telegram and express mail to assert its rights against the defendant Houtai Company, but the plaintiff did not file the lawsuit with the court until October 4, 1996. According to Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's "Certain Provisions on Issues Concerning Guarantees in the Trial of Economic Contract Dispute Cases," the defendant no longer bears guarantee liability.

The Siming District People's Court of Xiamen found through trial: On February 15, 1995, the plaintiff International Bank, the defendant Houtai Company, and the defendant Xiaosheng Company entered into a tripartite "Foreign Exchange Comprehensive Loan Facility Loan Contract" stipulating that International Bank would lend HKD 800,000 to Houtai Company. The loan term was from February 15, 1995, to May 15 of the same year. The annual loan interest rate was to be adjusted according to financial market conditions, at the Hong Kong dollar loan prime rate P+2%. If the borrower failed to repay the loan and interest as agreed, the lender had the right to compound interest on the overdue interest, and for the overdue portion of the loan, an additional 20% interest would be charged on the original interest rate. Xiaosheng Company provided joint and several liability guarantee for the loan. Article 3 of the "Guarantee Letter" issued by Xiaosheng Company to International Bank stipulated: "This guarantee letter shall remain in full force and effect until all principal, interest, overdue interest, and other expenses owed by the borrower to the lender under the loan contract are fully discharged." Article 8 stipulated: "This guarantee letter shall automatically terminate upon the full repayment of all amounts owed by the borrower to the lender under the loan contract." After the three parties signed and sealed the loan contract, International Bank made a loan of HKD 800,000 to Houtai Company as agreed. After the loan matured, Houtai Company failed to repay the loan and interest as agreed. Despite multiple demands by International Bank, Houtai Company only repaid the interest up to December 31, 1995; Xiaosheng Company also did not perform its guarantee obligation.

It was further found that on August 21, 1995, the defendant Xiaosheng Company notified the plaintiff International Bank in writing by telegram and express mail to assert its rights against the defendant Houtai Company. International Bank received the said correspondence, but did not file the lawsuit with the court until October 5, 1996.

The Siming District People's Court of Xiamen held: The "Foreign Exchange Comprehensive Loan Facility Loan Contract" signed by the plaintiff International Bank, the defendant Houtai Company, and the defendant Xiaosheng Company was legally valid and effective, and the parties should perform their obligations in accordance with the law. International Bank had performed its lending obligation as agreed, but Houtai Company failed to repay the loan as agreed. Pursuant to Article 106, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Houtai Company should bear civil liability for breach of contract. In accordance with Article 16 of the "Regulations on Loan Contracts," International Bank had the right to demand repayment of the loan within a specified period and to impose default interest at the bank's prescribed rate. Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Fa Fa (1994) No. 8 "Certain Provisions on Issues Concerning Guarantees in the Trial of Economic Contract Dispute Cases" provides: "Where a guarantee contract does not stipulate a period for the guarantee liability, or the stipulation is unclear, the guarantor shall bear the guarantee liability within the period during which the guaranteed party bears liability. If, after the expiration of the performance period of the main contract, the guarantor requests in writing that the creditor file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration against the guaranteed party, and the creditor fails to exercise its right of action within one month after receiving the written request, the guarantor shall no longer bear the guarantee liability." Xiaosheng Company's defense argument that it could be released from the guarantee liability had factual basis and legal support and could be adopted. Accordingly, on December 12, 1996, the Siming District People's Court of Xiamen ruled:

1. The defendant Houtai Company shall, within three days from the effective date of this judgment, repay the plaintiff International Bank the loan principal of HKD 800,000 and the interest and default interest from January 1, 1996, until the date of full repayment, at the interest rate stipulated in the loan contract.

2. The plaintiff International Bank's claim against the defendant Xiaosheng Company is dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the plaintiff International Bank, dissatisfied, filed an appeal with the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province. The appeal argued: The period of guarantee liability refers to the period during which the guarantor bears the guarantee liability as provided by law or agreed by the parties. Therefore, whether the period of guarantee liability is clearly stipulated should not be measured by whether there is a specific year, month, or day. Article 3 of the guarantee letter issued by Xiaosheng Company to the appellant on February 15, 1995, clearly states: "This guarantee letter is an irrevocable and continuing full liability guarantee. This guarantee letter shall remain in full force and effect until all principal, interest, overdue interest, and other expenses owed by the borrower to your bank under the loan contract are fully discharged." As long as the parties clearly stipulate when the guarantee liability will end, the period should be deemed clear. Therefore, this case should be governed by Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's "Certain Provisions on Issues Concerning Guarantees in the Trial of Economic Contract Dispute Cases," which provides: "Where a guarantee contract stipulates a period for the guarantee liability, the guarantor shall bear the guarantee liability within the stipulated period." The appellant requested the reversal of the original judgment, seeking an order for the borrower to repay the loan principal, interest, and overdue default interest; a judgment ordering Xiaosheng Company to assume joint and several guarantee liability for this debt; and an order that the appellees bear all litigation costs of this case.

The appellee Houtai Company, after being duly summoned, did not appear in court to participate in the proceedings.

The appellee Xiaosheng Company argued: The original judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law, and the appellant's appeal against Xiaosheng Company should be dismissed, and the original judgment should be affirmed.

The Xiamen Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance:

The loan contract signed by the three parties was legally valid and effective. The appellant International Bank performed its lending obligation as agreed, and the appellee Houtai Company should have repaid the loan as agreed. The focus of the dispute in this appeal was whether the appellee Xiaosheng Company could be released from its guarantee liability. The key to resolving this issue was whether the guarantee letter issued by Xiaosheng Company to International Bank clearly stipulated the period of guarantee liability.

The period of guarantee liability should be a fixed time frame, i.e., with clear start and end dates. Without such a time frame, it is impossible to determine when the obligor should perform its obligation or whether the performance constitutes a breach. In the stipulation of Article 3 of the guarantee letter in this case, because the actual repayment date of the borrower could not be determined, the period of the guarantor's guarantee liability could not be determined either. Such a stipulation was uncertain and had no practical significance in operation. Guarantee liability and the period of guarantee liability are two different concepts; clarity of guarantee liability does not equate to clarity of the period of guarantee liability. Therefore, the stipulation in this article fell precisely within the situation referred to in Article 11 of the "Certain Provisions on Issues Concerning Guarantees in the Trial of Economic Contract Dispute Cases." The judicial interpretation, addressing situations where the period of guarantee liability is not stipulated or is unclearly stipulated, provides for a period during which the guarantor may exercise its right of exhortation against the creditor, which is beneficial in urging the creditor to timely exercise its rights and the guarantor to timely perform its obligations. Under the circumstances where the period of guarantee liability was unclearly stipulated, Xiaosheng Company notified International Bank in writing by telegram and express mail to assert its rights against Houtai Company. However, International Bank, as the creditor, ignored its own rights and, after receiving the communication from Xiaosheng Company, failed to file a lawsuit within the prescribed period as requested in the communication, and did not file the lawsuit until October 1996, which had exceeded the period of exhortation. Xiaosheng Company's guarantee liability should be discharged. The original trial found clear facts, correctly applied the law, rendered an appropriate judgment, and the trial procedure was lawful; thus, the original judgment should be affirmed. The appellant's grounds for appeal were unsustainable and should be dismissed.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court ruled on October 22, 1997:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.
